Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-17 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Samir Khan (Redwood AE), Lina Torres (Redwood SE), Mark Ellis (Emberly - Head of Platform), Priya Nair (Emberly - SRE), Carlos Mendez (Emberly - Security), Asha Patel (Emberly - Eng Manager)

AUTO-SUMMARY (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Discovery focused on reliability, incident tolerance, multi-region routing and fallback policies.
- Emberly needs SLA ~99.9-99.95, predictable failover between regions, RBAC and KMS for keys, and audit logs.
- Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options; preferred Dedicated pilot + Private network for production.
- Next steps: SOC2/KMS docs, run benchmark, share pricing + deployment checklist.

[00:00] Samir (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining uh really appreciate you taking the time. Quick intros, we'll keep this as a discovery to understand your reliability constraints and incident tolerance needs and then Lina will cover the technical bits.
[00:18] Mark (Emberly): Yep thanks. Mark here, head of platform, Priya and Carlos are on for infra and security, and Asha from the payments team. We're trying to understand how Redwood would behave during outages and if we can meet our SLAs.
[00:28] Lina (SE): Great, mm-hmm. We usually go through traffic patterns, failure modes, and then routing/fallback policies. Quick question: are you currently running inference in-house or on a managed API?
[00:38] Asha (Emberly): We're hybrid \u2014 some endpoints on OpenAI for chatbot stuff, and an internal GPU pool for higher-sensitivity inference. Latency target for customer-facing flows is 200ms p95, internal processes can tolerate up to 1s.
[00:52] Priya (SRE): Our peak QPS is around 650 requests per minute for the fraud model, spiky around promos. We need failover within 60s to a different region and RTO under 5 minutes for critical flows.
[01:12] Samir: Good, that's helpful. When you say failover within 60s, are you expecting automatic DNS-level routing, or app-level fallback where you call a different endpoint?
[01:25] Priya: Mostly we'd like the platform to do it so transparent routing. We don't want to change our client logic during an incident.
[01:32] Lina: Understood. Redwood supports policy-based routing \u2014 you can set region preference, latency thresholds, and cost tiers. If a region violates SLOs we'll route to the next available compatible model. We also support canary and circuit-breaker style fallbacks.
[01:52] Carlos (Security): How do you handle data egress during cross-region failover? We have to ensure PII stays in approved regions.
[02:02] Lina: Good question. We have region-aware routing and sticky residency controls \u2014 you can restrict data to certain regions; for fallbacks that would cross boundaries, we can set policies to only route to compliant regions or to a model variant that runs in all approved regions. There's also an option for encryption-at-rest with customer-managed KMS/HSM.
[02:26] Carlos: Do you have HSM integration? We need hardware-backed keys for production.
[02:30] Samir: Yes, we support KMS and HSM integrations \u2014 I'll send the integration notes and our SOC2/ISO artifacts. We also support audit logging at the token/request level in Redwood Console.
[02:45] Mark: What's the tradeoff if we set up Dedicated vs Hosted? Security team leans Dedicated/private, but cost and time-to-prod are concerns.
[02:58] Lina: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, VPC peering, and more predictable throughput. Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) gives the most control for compliance. Hosted is fastest to start and we offer configurable fallbacks and multi-region routing, but for strict residency and HSM you probably want Dedicated or Private.
[03:20] Asha: For payment flows, even small latency spikes can impact conversions. Can Redwood do model variant fallback \u2014 like fall back to a smaller quantized model in the same region before crossing region boundaries?
[03:34] Lina: Yeah \u2014 you can define a fallback chain: primary model (e.g., rwinf-large) -> quantized lower-latency model (rwinf-compact) -> cross-region if allowed. That way you avoid cross-region egress unless necessary. Note: transcription may say 'Red wood' or 'r-win-f' sometimes, sorry if naming is odd.
[03:55] Priya: That fallback chain sounds good. How fast can the KV cache repopulate when failing over? In previous setups we saw cold cache penalties.
[04:06] Lina: We do prefix/K-V cache replication for session affinity within region; cross-region cold starts will happen but we can warm via pre-populate strategies during failover windows. Also configure shorter TTLs for non-critical caches to reduce staleness. Some of our customers pre-warm with synthetic traffic during DR tests.
[04:26] Mark: SLA talk \u2014 we need 99.9% for non-critical flows and 99.95% for payments. Can you meet that on Hosted?
[04:35] Samir: Hosted SLA is 99.9 by default for paid tiers; Dedicated can be negotiated to 99.95 with reserved capacity and an SLA addendum. We'll align metrics and error budgets in the contract.
[04:50] Carlos: On auditability \u2014 we need immutable logs for inference requests and key access. Is log retention configurable?
[04:58] Lina: Yes, retention is configurable per-account; logs can be exported to your S3 or to SIEM via syslog, and we support tamper-evident appenders. We also support RBAC and SAML/SSO for user access.
[05:14] Priya: Network specifics \u2014 if we go Dedicated, how do you handle VPC peering and egress? We need private connectivity, no public internet.
[05:24] Lina: We do VPC peering and private endpoints. For Dedicated there's an option for private control plane or a customer-managed control plane in Private deployments. We'll provide a deployment checklist covering subnet ranges, NATs, route tables, and security groups.
[05:40] Mark: What about fallback latency guarantees? If primary region is degraded, how soon can we expect the next region to pick up and return to p95 200ms?
[05:50] Lina: It depends on data locality and cache warming. In practice \u2014 with pre-warm and proper routing \u2014 customers see failover within 30-90s and p95 within 1-3x of normal latency until caches warm. Dedicated with replicated KV caches will be faster.
[06:12] Asha: Are there throttles or quota behaviors we should be aware of during a widespread failover? We don't want a sudden spike to exhaust capacity.
[06:20] Samir: We have adaptive throttling and quota enforcement per-customer and per-route; you can set circuit-breaker thresholds and automatic shedding policies. During capacity constraints we can route to lower-cost model variants to reduce token consumption.
[06:36] Priya: We also have legal/regulatory constraints \u2014 some transactions' data can't leave EU. Can we set per-route residency?
[06:44] Lina: Yes, policy granularity includes per-route residency. You can mark routes as EU-only, and the platform will only choose model endpoints in EU regions or the on-prem variant.
[06:56] Carlos: One more security question \u2014 when routing across regions do you re-encrypt with the destination region KMS or keep the same key? We must ensure key material doesn't leave the region.
[07:06] Lina: For crypto we support bring-your-own-key and also region-scoped keys. In cross-region fallback, you can choose to either block non-compliant routing, or use a region-local re-encrypt flow. We'll document options in the security pack.
[07:26] Samir: I'll drop our security pack and HSM docs after this meeting.
[07:32] Mark: Great. On the testing side \u2014 we want to run an end-to-end failover test that simulates losing a primary region; what does Redwood need from us to run that?
[07:41] Lina: We'll need sample traffic, peak QPS, auth tokens for a sandbox account, and network connectivity for the agent if you're validating VPC peering. We'll supply a test plan, and propose a 48-hour test window to observe failover and steady-state.
[07:58] Priya: We'll provide synthetic traces and a replay of typical traffic including spike scenarios.
[08:05] Asha: Observability \u2014 does Console show per-token latency and trace IDs so we can wire into our tracing?
[08:12] Lina: Yes, per-request traces and token-level cost breakdowns, and an API to stream traces to your tracing backend. There's also per-model dashboards.
[08:23] Mark: Quick question on billing during failover \u2014 if you route to a model variant in a different region with higher unit cost, how's that billed?
[08:31] Samir: Billing follows the active model endpoint and region pricing. You can configure fallback cost ceilings to prevent surprise charges: e.g., never route to >x cost per token without manual approval.
[08:43] Carlos: On the Dedicated pilot \u2014 what's the timeline? We need to align procurement.
[08:49] Samir: For a Dedicated pilot we typically do a 4-6 week ramp: initial network setup and creds, pilot for pre-prod with traffic mirroring for 2 weeks, then run failover tests and finalize SLA in week 4-6. Procurement timelines vary.
[09:05] Priya: What about multi-region active-active vs active-passive? Which does Redwood recommend?
[09:12] Lina: Active-active is ideal but more complex (replication, consistency). Many customers run active-passive with fast failover and rely on caching/replication for near-ss consistency. For payments, if you need strict locality we recommend active-passive with synchronous replication or an on-prem control plane.
[09:34] Mark: Any known gotchas? We had issues previously with KV cache thrash during failover where customers saw duplicated sessions.
[09:41] Lina: Yep \u2014 that's a common pattern. We recommend session affinity, idempotency keys, and short TTLs during cutover. Also, the fallback chain should prefer local quantized models before cross-region to minimize egress.
[09:56] Asha: Can we get rate-limits per-route so payment endpoints have stricter throttling than general chat?
[10:01] Samir: Absolutely, per-route quotas and token caps are supported.
[10:06] Priya: One more \u2014 do you support healthcheck hooks so our infra can probe Redwood endpoints and trigger our own failover?
[10:13] Lina: Yes, we expose health endpoints and metrics; you can integrate them into your monitoring to trigger playbooks. We also provide webhooks for incident notifications and a timeline view in Console.
[10:26] Samir: Let's quickly flesh out the hypothetical failover scenario for payments: primary EU region goes down, policy should first try compact model in EU, then if compact fails or is saturated, fail to EU-second region if allowed, else block or degrade gracefully. Is that roughly what you want?
[10:44] Carlos: Yes, but we want a final safety gate \u2014 block cross-border route for payment objects unless explicitly approved.
[10:51] Lina: That fits our per-route residency gating.
[10:56] Mark: For the benchmark Lina's going to run \u2014 can we include a scenario where one region is artificially slowed to emulate network partition?
[11:04] Lina: Yes, we can simulate increased latency and also simulate pod/node drains to test circuit-breakers.
[11:12] Asha: When switching between model variants do you preserve conversation context? We use chat history to maintain continuity.
[11:20] Lina: We maintain KV cache where possible; switching variants within the same architecture preserves context better. Cross-architecture fallbacks may need summarization or context re-encoding. We'll document expected delta for each fallback chain.
[11:36] Priya: Ok, security again \u2014 who can access logs? They need to be RBAC-protected and show the actor.
[11:44] Samir: RBAC with SAML SSO and per-role log access is standard. We also have an audit trail with user identity for actions.
[11:52] Mark: For our procurement team, we'll need sample contract language around SLA credits and data residency \u2014 is that standard?
[11:59] Samir: We have standard addenda for Dedicated and Private that include SLA terms and credits. I'll attach sample language.
[12:06] Lina: Quick note: sometimes our speech recognition in recordings confuses 'KV cache' as 'K V cash' \u2014 so in docs you'll see that.
[12:14] (short laughter)
[12:18] Samir: Any blockers for moving to a pilot?
[12:22] Asha: Procurement sign-off, security review of SOC2 and HSM, and a successful benchmark are the main gates.
[12:30] Carlos: Also need a clear incident response runbook for Redwood-managed incidents.
[12:35] Lina: We provide an incident runbook template and post-incident reports; for Dedicated we also offer a direct pager escalation.
[12:44] Mark: Great \u2014 let's talk about pricing. Can you give a rough range for Dedicated pilot?
[12:50] Samir: Roughly a monthly reserved commitment based on GPU type. For pilots we normally do a smaller committed baseline + burst. I'll share specific numbers in the follow-up.
[13:03] Priya: During the pilot we'd like to mirror traffic rather than route live \u2014 is that supported?
[13:08] Lina: Yes, traffic mirroring is supported for non-destructive tests. You can send copies to Redwood and we won't affect production until you flip the route.
[13:16] Mark: One more operational question \u2014 how do you handle upgrades and rollouts that might impact latency?
[13:24] Lina: We do canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic rollback on regressions. Console surfaces model-level perf deltas and we can pin to previous versions.
[13:35] Samir: Ok, we're at about half-hour mark \u2014 should we recap next steps?
[13:40] Mark: Yeah great.
[13:42] Samir: Recap: Samir sends SOC2/HSM docs and sample contract language (due 2026-02-19). Lina will run a 48hr benchmark plan and test harness \u2014 she'll need sample traffic and credentials (plan due 2026-02-21). Priya to provide traffic patterns and peak qps (due 2026-02-20). We'll schedule the VPC deep-dive on 2026-02-25. Any additions?
[14:04] Carlos: Add the incident runbook review to the VPC deep-dive agenda.
[14:09] Samir: Noted.
[14:12] Asha: Also include cost control policies in the deployment checklist \u2014 fallback cost ceilings.
[14:18] Lina: Will do.
[14:22] Mark: Sounds good.
[14:27] (brief side discussion about procurement deadlines 1:20 left out)
[14:45] Priya: One nit \u2014 can we ensure billing visibility at token-level per-route so our finance team can allocate spend?
[14:52] Samir: Yes token-level cost breakdown per-route is available in Console and via API exports.
[14:59] Mark: Perfect. We're good on time \u2014 thanks everybody.
[15:05] Samir: Thanks \u2014 we'll follow up with docs and the benchmark timeline.
